title: After-action: node CPU surge + CNI flap
content:
Executive summary:

On 2025-10-30 03:41 UTC several production clusters began experiencing increased pod start latency and API errors. By 03:46 UTC a set of nodes in us-west1-b showed sustained kernel-level CPU utilization spikes, followed by repeated CNI plugin restarts and a correlated spike in conntrack table usage. The cascading effect caused the kubelet to report node-not-ready for a subset of nodes, which triggered a scheduling backlog and client-facing errors (500s on inference control plane) for ~14 minutes for affected zones. Mitigation reverted traffic off the impacted nodes and applied a temporary conntrack tuning.

Detection and alerts that fired:
- 03:43 UTC: pod-start-latency alert (p95 > 8s) for model-serving namespace.
- 03:44 UTC: kubelet:node-not-ready count +2 in us-west1-b.
- 03:45 UTC: host:cpu-system > 85% on nodes gke-inference-*-pool-a.
- 03:46 UTC: cni-plugin restarts detected (flannel/pluggerd) from node-exporter logs.
- 03:48 UTC: conntrack-saturation warning (conntrack count > 75% of table size).

Impact (observed):
- SLO blips for request latency and elevated 500s targeted to control plane (inference job scheduling endpoints).
- 7 nodes had transient NotReady transitions; 2 of those required manual kubelet restart to return to Ready.
- ~120 pods evicted and rescheduled across zones; some long-running jobs requeued.
- Total customer-visible disruption window ~14 minutes; increased orchestration retries through following 45 minutes.

Initial on-call actions (timeline):
- 03:42 UTC: On-call (Ava) acknowledges page and opens incident channel.
- 03:44 UTC: Scoped to CPU spike + scheduling errors, removed new batch jobs (cron model-sync) from cluster in us-west1-b via kubectl scale --replicas=0 -n infra batchsync-job.
- 03:46 UTC: Shifted control-plane traffic via service weight override (rollout-svc: 0.0 -> canary fallback region) to reduce new scheduling pressure.
- 03:48 UTC: Set conntrack max to 200000 temporarily on affected nodes: sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000 and bumped hashsize; applied via gcloud ssh loop.
- 03:52 UTC: Observed cni restarts drop off and conntrack headroom restored, node conditions cleared progressively.

Root cause analysis (hypothesis and evidence):
Hypothesis: A background cron (batch model-sync) that had a recently changed concurrency parameter started generating a burst of short-lived connections to backend services causing kernel CPU system time to spike (conntrack churn). The CNI plugin (flannel) attempted to reconcile state during the burst, leading to repeated restarts on heavy conntrack churn. The kubelet experienced increased pressure due to pod churn and transient CNI failures, marking nodes NotReady.
Evidence supporting hypothesis:
- Process accounting shows spikes in kernel CPU and nf_conntrack churn during the incident window; top and perf showed high syscall time (netfilter related) on affected nodes.
- Cron job replicas in us-west1-b had scaled from 3->12 in a recent rollout (PR 3378) with a mis-typed env var controlling concurrency; rollout was flagged in linked PR.
- conntrack table usage correlated tightly with new pod lifecycle events in the model-serving namespace.
- The nodes that flipped NotReady all ran flannel v0.13.1 and had default conntrack limits (65536).
Evidence against other causes:
- No kernel panic, no OOM-kill logs for kubelet.
- etcd health remained green; master control plane not impacted.

Why CNI restarts?
CNI process logs show repeated timeouts during iptables programming under heavy conntrack churn; flannel appears to have a code path that retries and exits on timing assumptions which in this case lead to repeated restarts (observed 3-5 restarts/node).

Mitigations applied (short term):
- Scaled down the misbehaving cron (workaround to stop connection bursts).
- Increased conntrack table limits on impacted nodes to provide headroom.
- Temporarily drained the worst affected nodes and rotated new instances with updated sysctl settings via instance template patch.
- Rolled traffic using weight overrides to reduce scheduling load to region.

Persistent fixes and follow-ups (action items):
- (Owner: Priya) Revert or patch the cron concurrency change in PR 3378 and add CI checks to prevent env var typos. Target: 2025-11-05.
- (Owner: Diego) Add a preflight check in deploy pipelines that validates expected concurrency ranges for infra cron jobs (hook in CD). Target: 2025-11-12.
- (Owner: Ethan) Patch flannel config or upgrade to v0.14.x in a canary cluster; verify iptables programming latency under conntrack churn. Target: 2025-11-20.
- (Owner: SRE Platform) Increase default conntrack limits in node base images from 65536 -> 200000 and add as a sysctl-managed parameter with rollout. Target: 2025-12-01.
- Add a dashboard and alert for conntrack usage per-node and a synthetic that simulates high-connection churn to validate CNI resilience. (Owner: eng-observability).

Runbook draft: rapid steps for on-call (short checklist)
- Detect: Check pod-start-latency, node-not-ready, host:cpu-system.
- Scope: Identify affected nodes: kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep NotReady.
- Immediate mitigation (if conntrack is near max): sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000; echo 200000 | sudo tee /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max. Confirm with cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count.
- If CNI restarting: check /var/log/containers/*cni* and journalctl -u kubelet -u flanneld.
- If pod churn from cron job or job controller: kubectl -n <ns> get jobs, scale down controllers (kubectl scale --replicas=0).
- Fallback: cordon and drain problematic nodes and restart kubelet if node remains NotReady after CNI stabilizes. kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data then restart kubelet: sudo systemctl restart kubelet.
- Communication: open incident channel, update #sre-oncall with region and mitigation steps.

Commands run during incident (scratchpad):
- kubectl -n infra scale job/batchsync-job --replicas=0
- for n in $(gcloud compute instances list --filter="name~'gke-inference.*pool-a'" --zones us-west1-b --format="value(NAME)"); do gcloud compute ssh $n --zone us-west1-b --command "sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000"; done
- kubectl cordon gke-inference-a-07 && kubectl drain gke-inference-a-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
- journalctl -u flanneld -n 200 --no-pager | sed -n '1,200p' > /tmp/flannel-logs-0310.txt

Monitoring and dashboards to add or tune:
- Per-node conntrack headroom gauge with 80%/90%/95% thresholds.
- CPU time split (user/sys/irq) for nodes in pods churn tests.
- CNI restart count metric emitting to monitoring.
- Pod admission latency for create/start as synthetic per namespace.

Post-incident notes and miscellaneous observations (on-call style):
- We relied on manual SSH+sysctl; consider adding a remediation playbook as an automation (k8s daemonset that increases nf_conntrack_max when threshold crossed).
- The bottleneck wasn't user CPU but kernel syscalls — traditional CPU autoscaling rules (user) would not have caught this. Consider adding host:cpu-system in autoscale heuristics for emergency replacement triggers.
- There is an opportunity to harden flannel's handling of rapid conntrack churn or switch to Canal/Calico in high-connection namespaces. Need bench results.

Open questions (unresolved):
- Why did flannel choose restart instead of backoff? Is this a known regression in v0.13.1? (Action: Diego to confirm with flannel changelog and vendor).
- Should conntrack limits be raised cluster-wide or targeted only to high-connection node pools? (Tradeoff: memory).
- Are there other jobs with similar misconfigured concurrency? Add linting to look for env variables named *_CONCURRENCY in repos.

Appendix: raw timelines & snippets (trimmed)
- 03:40:12 UTC: cron-model-sync scaled to 12 replicas as part of rollout.
- 03:42:50 UTC: spike in SYN_RECV and ESTABLISHED sockets on 10.128.x.x.
- 03:45:04 UTC: cni-plugin: failed to program iptables rules: timeout
- 03:46:07 UTC: kubelet reports NetworkUnavailable -> NotReady (5 nodes)
- 03:55:18 UTC: nodes clear, conntrack headroom restored, pods start succeeding

Notes to future on-call: keep incident channel open for 30m after nodes clear to catch any delayed churn. If you escalate to SEV1, move to executive paging and follow company incident comms template.

Related artifacts: see linked JIRA SRE-4821 for post-incident ticket with timeline export, PR 3378 for the cron change, and github PR 3378 discussion for rollout context.

Document history / authorship: initial draft by Ava Thompson (on-call) 2025-11-02; review comments from Diego and Priya 2025-11-10; updated with follow-up owners 2026-01-15.

Scratchy personal notes: felt odd that internal cron change slipped past staging checks. Need to spend 1-2 hours building a small preflight test harness that replays container start patterns (fast short-lived connections) to catch conntrack edge cases during deploys.
